title: I was just testing the new AI tool from OpenAI — GPT-5.3 Codex In Unity3D and the result honestly shocked me.
author: SumitDubey3
selftext:
In under 30 minutes, it created this game demo in Unity3D

If this is where AI is today, imagine the future…  
What used to take 6 months to a year might soon take just 2–3 months with small teams.

Do you think AAA-level games will soon be possible with small indie teams?

I’m currently testing different AI tools to see how far we can push AI in game development… and this is just the beginning

comments.author: blursed_1
comments.body:
So the issue with AI is context and hallucinations when making bigger projects. It's definitely a way to speed things up, but as you try to make a more complex or actually fun game; you'll soon find that actual programming and game design experience is required. 

That's why all "AI games" kind of look the same. They're either story-menu simulators or basic run and jump games.

comments.author: DragonfruitDecent862
comments.body:
Having found the insane game development potential from Claude Code, that allows claude to work directly in yoyr windows folders, i coded a pluin to unity based on a system i have for another game ebgine called synapse. It gives a LLM the ability to "see" and analyze all scene objects in the current unity scene, and can launch play mode and self loop diagnoise what should happen.         

I tried mcps long ago, but they were limited. Nowdays, you have have your coding agent that has access to your desktop (like claude code, gpts codex) actually make a intergration system that is uniquely tailored to your engine. I really recommend this, as a ai can find performance issues and problems , and math issues, without hours or days spent.  My custom game engine, made with claude, uses a full intergration system like this, and i made one for unity just recently. You can do it, but you need to know what makes a good intergration

replies.author: SumitDubey3
replies.body: Sounds great

replies.author: M4xs0n
replies.body: How is your way better than using a Software that already does this like Bezi? Would be interesting to know

replies.author: DragonfruitDecent862
replies.body: the issue with current models, is their standardization,  limiting the flexibility that they offer. Heres a good example. A tool that exists will offer a llm certain, rigid methods for what can be accessed, and how. Sometimes, and eventually, all clients dont offer the control your seeking. Bezi offers features that are great, but say you need  your ai to generate scripts, auto refresh manually the unity recomple, and then enter play mode and verify EVERY SINGLE game objects position and transform. Then based on that, define a new addon framework that simplifys this process.   A llm framework for gane engine access must work throught what is allowed by the plugin.    Hence, limiting.

replies.author: Cannabalistic-Muffin
replies.body: Verify object position and transform? Can’t you use a unity test runner for that? Seems very overkill to have deterministic validation done directly by an LLM

replies.author: DragonfruitDecent862
replies.body: We're doing validation due to the llm doing its own additions, for self checking. Unlike a human, it can handle about 10,000 different data streams at any given time. Its better than any human quantitative analysis. And it does this to validate complex game system additions, like range weapon arc testing, rpg stats triggers, ect.

replies.author: Cannabalistic-Muffin
replies.body:
I didn’t particularly mean, you setup your own test runner. The agent could set up its own test runner. If you have explicit validation logic (either designed by you or the LLM) that’s great. If you don’t, as you approach the context limit, the probability the LLM hallucinates increases. Explicit validation logic will never hallucinate. The only other way around this is by having a sub-agent that only handles the validation with an assumption the amount it needs to validate will never come close to its window.

But for that last part, depending on what API you’re using that’ll either cost money or will get you limited very quickly.

Unless money is no object or time is no object. Then you could probably let it do this hands off with good enough context management

replies.author: DragonfruitDecent862
replies.body: Very good analysis! You are correct.  Cli based llms rarely hallucinate ive noticed, at least not claude, as before they hit that context degration zone, they write the current project mission and memory to buffer, and clear their context automaticly. Ever since using a llm like this, no hallucinations. At least with the higher tiers of models.   Is this expensive at times? Oh yes, absolutely. Is it viable long term? Oh hell no. But its a great time saver if you have context to burn.

replies.author: DragonfruitDecent862
replies.body: Any machine can do this, but a hard requirement is a llm that can directly access a project folder on your physical machine. Or use a cliebt to allow a llm access to a folder directly. Either way, claude code cli, or openai codex are good examples. Even the pro, limited plans can do this. Just have a CLI based LLM.  Modern llms know how software systems are put together, and can even teach you how to make your own. But a LLMs original goal is Analysis and data gathering. You ask a llm to add digital probes where the efficency of the software code is needed, and then give it access, say a https cliebt or special puthon system to connect to those probes while you run the software. Like putting a high powered engine on a testing rack, and attacting physical probes to monitor temps, speed, rpms, you can do the same to software. Most human testers and devs wont do this, as this is hard to keep track of, but a llm can do millions of calculations in seconds. Its how i just recently got CATALYST engine to output actual game performance around 0.5ms per frame total, in vr. Unity and unreal average 10ms for vr. Lol. I had to do multiple tests to ensure the readings were accurate. With the probe system, claude code analyzed thr pipeline and made changes that now make unity or godot seem really, really slow. Need any help setting this up for your projects, let me know.
